newsitem.title: SPAIN: Seat makes profit after three years of losses.
newsitem.headline: Seat makes profit after three years of losses.

text.p: Volkswagen AG's Spanish subsidiary Seat said Tuesday it made a net profit of 5.34 billion pesetas ($37.3 million) in 1996 after three years of heavy losses.
Seat's performance was boosted by a series of exceptional items, including asset sales and subsidies, but the firm said it hoped to make a profit on the strength of its own operations in 1997.

"It's still early to make forecasts for 1997 but our target is to reach profits without any external aid and, according to data from the first part of the year, we seem to be in a position to do it," Chairman Alain de Smedt told a news conference.

In the two months to February this year, Seat's sales rose 32.5 percent to 114.84 billion pesetas ($803 million). Sales in 1996 rose to 607.3 billion pesetas ($4.2 billion) from 456.52 billion ($3.2 billion) in 1995.
Seat aims to raise production by more than 10 percent this year to 460,000 units, with sales growing at the same rate.

Seat's return to profits in 1996 marks the end of a black period in which its worst performance showed losses of 151.32 billion pesetas ($1.1 billion) in 1993. Those were reduced to losses of 29.47 billion ($206 million) in 1994 and 11.29 billion ($79 million) in 1995.
The company underwent a restructuring, which included concentration of production at its Martorell plant in Catalonia, as well as the sale of its Navarre plant to Volkswagen.
After the restructuring, the number of Seat employees has fallen to roughly 12,900 from more than 20,000 workers.
